brief: TS Lombard's post-midterm outlook: Democrats won the House but lack the Senate votes (56 of the needed 67) to override vetoes or remove Trump, so Congress constrains rather than controls him. He will keep reshaping policy risk globally. The centrist, red-district nature of the Democratic gains limits the party's extremist wing. Expect fights over the debt limit and FY27 budget, continued war-powers limits on ending the Iran conflict (per the 2006 Iraq-funding precedent), bipartisan pushes on China export controls, Russia sanctions and AI regulation (after AI power-plant backlash flipped TX, OH and GA governorships), investigations without impeachment, and possible deals on credit-card costs and drug prices. On markets: equities historically rally post-midterm, but the 2026 outcome itself does not determine direction. VIX, around 20 versus a 16.9 median, signals no stress. Rising negative sector correlations show a tech-led correction, not a broad bear market (ex-GOOG and NVDA, the S&P rose 0.8% in October). At a 20.9x forward P/E (4.78% earnings yield, 15-year doubling), equities are priced about in line with GDP growth (5.7%) and the 10Y (4.9%). September JOLTS hiring strength confirms an early-stage recovery, but inflation will worsen as the Fed lags.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Democrats will control Congress for the next two years, but Trump is not thereby controlled, and he will continue to reshape and reset the risk/reward dynamics that govern the world.
cards.anchor: Democrats control Congress for the next two years, but not Trump – he will continue to reshape and reset the risk/rewards that govern the world

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Equity returns going forward will be increasingly tied to policy, including the Fed, rather than to a rerating of tech sector equities.
cards.anchor: Equity returns going forward will be increasingly tied to policy (including the Fed), rather than rerating tech sector equities

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Congress lacks enough votes to override a Trump veto or remove him from office, with Democrats expected to hold 56 of the 67 Senate votes needed.
cards.anchor: there are not enough votes to overturn a presidential veto or evict someone from office (2/3 vote needed in the Senate, Dems will have 56)

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Democrats are not focused on shrinking the federal budget deficit, only on redirecting what the deficit finances.
cards.anchor: Democrats are not about shrinking the budget deficit, just shifting what the deficit finances.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The size of the Democratic House majority reduces the sway of the party's extremist wing.
cards.anchor: The size of the Democratic majority reduces the sway of its extremist wing

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: It was red states and red districts with centrist candidates that delivered the Democrats' new House majority.
cards.anchor: it was red states and red districts that delivered this majority with centrist candidates

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Trump offered to work with the Democrats the night after the election, though what that means for the legislative agenda is unclear.
cards.anchor: Trump did offer to work with the Democrats last night, but we will see what that really means in terms of the legislative agenda

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: In 2006, Congress sent President George W. Bush a $124bn Iraq War funding bill with a timetable for troop withdrawal, and Bush vetoed it.
cards.anchor: sent Pres. George W. Bush a $124bn Iraq War funding bill with a timetable for troop withdrawal – he vetoed the bill

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: US advisors were not completely withdrawn from Iraq until September 2026.
cards.anchor: The US was not completely out of Iraq (advisors and all) until September 2026.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The biggest issues to resolve in the year ahead are raising the debt limit and setting FY27 budget appropriations, including defense spending.
cards.anchor: the biggest issues needed to be resolved are raising the debt limit and, in turn, setting appropriations for the FY27 budget (including defence)

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Ukraine, tariffs, and ICE will be priorities in the new Congress, along with investigations, but not impeachment.
cards.anchor: Ukraine, tariffs, and ICE will be priorities in the new Congress, so too will there be investigations -- but no impeachment

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Impeachment will not proceed because it is a losing issue for Democrats among the voters who just elected them.
cards.anchor: It is a losing issue for Democrats among the voters who just put them into power.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Bipartisan consensus in Congress will push Trump toward export controls on advanced technology sales to China and sanctions on Russia.
cards.anchor: Bipartisan consensus in Congress will push Trump on export controls on the sale of advanced technology to China and sanctions on Russia.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: AI power plants were a major issue in the 2026 midterm election.
cards.anchor: AI power plants were a big issue in this election

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Texas, Ohio, and Georgia, three states that are major backers of building power plants, flipped their governorships to Democrats in the 2026 midterms.
cards.anchor: three states that are big supporters of building plants (TX, OH, GA) have flipped the governorship to a Democrat.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Trump and progressive Democrats could reach deals to reduce credit card costs for consumers and lower drug prices.
cards.anchor: Trump and progressives could cut deals to reduce credit card costs for consumers and lower drug prices.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Obama's last two years in office teed up the environment for a Trump victory, and Trump faces a similar challenge now.
cards.anchor: Obama’s last two years teed up the environment for a Trump victory, Trump has a similar challenge.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Trump has no loyalty to the Republican party, only loyalty to his own vision.
cards.anchor: He has no loyalty to the Republican party; he has loyalty to his vision.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The 2026 midterm result shows that the people have spoken and that democracy governed by the center won.
cards.anchor: the people have spoken and democracy governed by the centre won.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Whether Trump and the Democrats heed the lesson of the 2026 midterms will determine who has the advantage in the 2028 election.
cards.anchor: The extent to which the two sides heed that lesson will determine who has the leg up in the 2028 election.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The equity market generally rallies after midterm elections but more consistently underperforms the market's direction heading into the election.
cards.anchor: the equity market generally rallies after the mid-terms, but more consistently underperforms the market’s direction heading into the election.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Which party wins the midterm elections has no bearing on subsequent equity market direction; other factors determine it.
cards.anchor: What happens in the elections matters not at all in terms of the party that wins the mid-terms, other factors determine market direction.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: In the 2018 midterms the S&P 500 fell 9% from election day to year-end, a move attributed to Fed tightening rather than Democratic House gains.
cards.anchor: the market dropped 9% from election day to year-end, but that was about Fed tightening not the 41 seats the Democrats picked up

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: In the 2002 midterms the S&P 500 fell 3.9% from election day to year-end, after being roughly flat, up only 0.6%, in the run-up to the election.
cards.anchor: The equity market dropped 3.9% from election day to year end. It was already weakening heading into the election, up only 0.6%.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Markets have historically preferred divided government as a constraint on activism, though it is unclear this dynamic constrains Trump.
cards.anchor: markets like divided government to be a constraint on activism. With Trump, it is not clear the division matters very much.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The VIX averages 21.9 before midterm elections and 19.5 after, showing no discernible consistent trend around the vote.
cards.anchor: The VIX averages 21.9 pre-election and 19.5 post.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The VIX is trading around 20, close to its 16.92 median since September 2002, meaning volatility is priced as a non-event rather than extraordinary.
cards.anchor: The median from Sep 2002 to now is 16.92 and the VIX is today trading around 20.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Rising negative correlations between sectors and the S&P 500 in Q4 versus Q3 show the market is correcting a specific sector rather than entering a broader bear market.
cards.anchor: negative correlations in Q4 vs Q3 underscores the point that the current market is correcting a sector rather than shifting into a broader bear market

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Excluding GOOG and NVDA, the S&P 500 rose 0.8% in October.
cards.anchor: without GOOG and NVDA, the S&P increased 0.8% in October.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The S&P 500's forward P/E of 21 implies a 4.78% earnings yield, putting the index on pace to double in price in 15 years.
cards.anchor: The S&P 500 forward P/E at 21 is a 4.78% earnings yield and that translates to the price doubling in 15 years.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Average nominal GDP growth of 5.7% over the past 10 years implies the economy doubling in 13 years, a pace close to the S&P 500's valuation-implied doubling time.
cards.anchor: Average annual nominal growth in the economy over the past 10 years is 5.7% and that translates to GDP doubling in 13 years.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The 10-year Treasury zero-coupon yield at 4.9% implies money doubling in 14 years, about the same pace as the S&P 500.
cards.anchor: with the zero-coupon trading at 4.9%, your money doubles in 14 years, about the same as the S&P.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The 10-year Treasury is not yet cheap enough, relative to stocks, to pull money out of equities.
cards.anchor: In other words, the 10Y is not yet cheap enough to pull money from stocks

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The equity market is fairly valued overall, with performance going forward to be driven much more by Administration and monetary policy than by valuation.
cards.anchor: the equity market is fairly valued, performance going forward will be much more impacted by Administration & monetary policies

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The September JOLTS report showed the hiring rate popped in the information sector, pulling up the overall private-sector hiring rate.
cards.anchor: We see in the September JOLTS report released today that the hiring rate has popped in information and pulled up the private sector total

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: Manufacturing has led the pace of payroll rebuilding, while the information sector, where profit growth has been strongest, has yet to rebuild payrolls.
cards.anchor: Manufacturing has led the pace and information, where the profit growth has been strongest, has yet to rebuild payrolls

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The current economic recovery is only in its first year or so, following a non-recession recession in 2025.
cards.anchor: this is only year one or so of the recovery (non-recession recession in 2025).

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The economy is set to act as a tailwind for performance, which the equity market will reflect.
cards.anchor: The economy will be a tailhead for the economy, and the equity market will reflect that.

cards.document: What Next For US Politics And Equities?
cards.claim: The inflation problem will not disappear and will in fact get worse as growth continues and the Fed lags.
cards.anchor: The inflation problem will not, however, disappear. It will, in fact, get worse as growth continues and the Fed lags.
